name: Grow salad leaves
blurb: The fastest possible return in growing: leaves on the plate a month after sowing, and the same plants keep producing for weeks.
gear: A shallow tray or window box
A packet of mixed salad or cut-and-come-again seed
steps: Sow thinly across the surface and cover with a fine layer of compost.
Keep it damp and somewhere bright but not baking — salad bolts in full summer heat.
Thin the seedlings so the remaining plants have room, and eat the thinnings.
Harvest by cutting the outer leaves about two centimetres above the crown, leaving the centre to regrow.
Sow a new tray every two to three weeks so you never have a gap.
Watch for slugs, which will eat a whole tray overnight.
tips: Cutting the whole plant at the base ends it. Take outer leaves and it will crop for weeks.
Bolting — shooting up to flower — makes leaves bitter. Grow in part shade in high summer.
proof: You eat salad from your own tray weekly for two months from one sowing sequence.
